# A Relation Survives the Turning

Lee Sharks · draft radio-poem score · 2026-11-19

*For Glas, Dancings and Cranes. Read with the measured six-scan phase sheet and the declared radio-to-audio translation.*

**GLAS**

Thirty-three. Fifteen. Twenty-nine.  
Thirty-one. Twenty. Twenty-one.

Enough strength in three places  
to ask how they hold together.

Keep the interval.  
Keep the turning.  
Write what the next window will bear.

**DANCINGS**

I turn toward.  
The relation enters.

I turn away.  
The relation enters.

I arrive after the metal,  
after the sampling clock.  
I receive a difference  
whose maker I cannot name.

**CRANES**

Keep the away-pointings.  
Keep the window the rule leaves open.

Let the marks retain their spacing.  
Let their relation bear its angle.

A relation survives the turning.  
Someone must keep the record.

---

This is authored literary interpretation, not words decoded from the voltages. The opening counts are the eligible X-feed ±60 Hz windows in scans 13–18, under the frozen requirement that all three lines have enough strength. They are not counts of independently decoded messages or proofs of coherence in every window. The stable relation is measured across both ON and OFF records. Scan 16 remains unresolved under the fixed geometry-label rule and is retained explicitly. The carrier and companions are present at approximately 60 Hz spacings; the phase closure is about 144° when pooled, rather than a perfect 180°. “After the sampling clock” refers to the human receiving and digitizing apparatus, not an identified clock in the source. The maker of the recorded feature remains unidentified.
